text:
Them 1: Hi, thanks for making the time, I know it is a busy week.
You: No problem at all, happy to be here. How is your week going so far?
Them 1: Pretty hectic, we have a board meeting on Thursday and everybody is scrambling.
You: That sounds familiar. Tell me a bit about what your support team looks like today.
Them 1: We are eleven people split across two shifts, mostly handling email and some chat, and it is getting out of hand.
You: Eleven agents is a good size for Relay. What are you using at the moment?
Them 1: A shared inbox plus a lot of spreadsheets, honestly. Nothing that deserves to be called a system.
You: Okay. And what would a good outcome look like for you in the next quarter?
Them 1: Faster first replies, and our director wants clear reporting. That is the main thing she keeps asking me for.
You: Understood. Let me walk you through how the inbox and the reporting fit together.
Them 1: Sure, go ahead.
You: Give me a moment to open the demo workspace on my screen.
You: So every conversation lands in one queue, you can assign it, tag it and see response times per agent on the dashboard.
Them 1: That sounds good. Before we go further I want to be sure about the money side, because pricing is the first thing finance will ask me.
Them 1: We would need eleven seats, and we would probably pay for the year upfront, so I am trying to get a feel for the price per seat on the Team plan.
You: Right, I will pull the numbers up for you in a second, bear with me.
Them 1: No rush. Finance wants a seat price and whether paying annually changes anything, because the budget is per year.
Them 1: And I assume the trial works on the same plan, we would like to try it before we commit anybody.
You: Absolutely, let me find the exact wording for the trial.
Them 1: Great. While you look, our security person also wants to join the next call, he is very particular.
You: Good, we love security people, they ask the best questions.
Them 1: He will want to know about single sign-on, our whole company logs in through SAML and he will not allow separate passwords.
Them 1: So the single sign-on setup and which plan has SAML sign-on is probably the biggest question for him, plus user provisioning if you have it.
You: That is a common requirement, I will make sure the right person is on the next call.
Them 1: Perfect. He also cares about where the data lives, we are in Germany so we want to keep conversation data inside the European Union.
You: Understood. We can pick the region when the workspace is created.
Them 1: Good. And how long do you keep our conversations? Our legal team has a rule about retention, they prefer thirty days at most for customer chats.
Them 1: So the data retention period and whether we can shorten it is something I need to take back to legal, they will ask about deleting old conversations from backups too.
You: Let me note that down, retention and backups.
Them 1: Thanks. Now, integrations. We live in Slack and our sales team uses Salesforce, so the connection to Slack and Salesforce matters.
You: Both are built in, you can switch them on from the settings page in a couple of clicks.
Them 1: Nice. And what about moving our old tickets, we have about two years of history in Zendesk.
You: We can import tickets, contacts and macros from Zendesk. Migration is not something we charge for.
Them 1: That would make my life much easier. How long does onboarding usually take for a team our size?
You: Most teams are live in about two weeks.
Them 1: That fits, we would want to be live before the end of next month.
You: Then we have plenty of time. Anything else on your list?
Them 1: Just the reporting, I think I would like to see that dashboard properly in a follow up, maybe with my director there.
You: Of course. Shall we put something in the diary for next week?
Them 1: Yes, Tuesday works well for us, in the morning if you can.
You: Tuesday morning it is. I will send an invite after this call.
Them 1: Wonderful. Thank you again, this was useful.
You: My pleasure, speak to you Tuesday.
